chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to me from 'Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Salamah, the companion of Al-Saburi, from Abu Al-Subbah Al-Kinani, who said:

I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Verily, there is a grave near you to which no anguished person goes without Allah removing his anguish and fulfilling his request. And verily, there are four thousand angels with him since the day his soul was taken, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping over him until the Day of Judgment. So whoever visits him, they accompany him; whoever falls ill, they visit him; and whoever dies, they follow his funeral procession.
ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of visiting the grave mentioned in Kamil al-Ziyarah regarding angels and relief from distress?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the intercessory power of Imam Husayn’s grave, noting that four thousand angels have remained in a state of perpetual mourning since his martyrdom, actively attending to the needs of visitors. This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the ongoing spiritual presence of the Imams, where their burial sites serve as conduits for divine relief (kashf al-kurba) and angelic accompaniment, reinforcing the concept of Ziyarat as a means of drawing closer to God through the Ahl al-Bayt.
